<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-content.mjs from Limitations.md. Edit the source in the Kanade repository, then run npm run sync. -->

Gaps in the lock screen, idle handling, polkit authentication and the SDDM login theme.

- The SDDM login screen theme is written for a Qt greeter on a login manager you already run; Kanade is not a greeter. Themes other than Kanade's own are best effort (see [SDDM](/integrations/sddm/)), and a picture set by hand in the overlay is not size-checked, which a Qt 5 greeter can choke on.
- Locking before sleep waits until niri says it holds the lock, which it says once every monitor on shows a lock screen. If it does not by logind's `InhibitDelayMaxSec`, sleep comes anyway, and the lock is asked again as the machine wakes: at once, then with a backoff, until it holds or you lock some other way. A lock niri is still confirming as the machine wakes is not asked for twice, so a password typed on the lock screen meanwhile is not dropped. The session was unlocked for the sleep itself, so anything it drew or played shows in that time.
- With no PAM service file (the `lock.pam_service` one, `login` by default, in `/etc/pam.d`, `/usr/lib/pam.d` or `/usr/etc/pam.d`), the lock is never asked, before sleep or after it: nothing could unlock it, and a lock that cannot be unlocked is worse than none. The machine then sleeps and wakes unlocked, and `kanade lock` refuses too. `kanade doctor` names the missing file. See [ADR 0025](https://github.com/0x1d1e/kanade/blob/main/docs/adr/0025-the-lock-screen-over-its-own-connection.md).
- An unlock sent just before sleep is asked over: the session unlocks for a moment, then locks again before sleep is let go, unless that outlasts logind's `InhibitDelayMaxSec`. Kanade sends the unlock under the same lock as sleep's gate, so only an unlock already sent races it. See [ADR 0025](https://github.com/0x1d1e/kanade/blob/main/docs/adr/0025-the-lock-screen-over-its-own-connection.md).
- The lock screen does not type the key that wakes monitors the `idle` Module powered off. It cannot know of monitors powered off any other way (`niri msg action power-off-monitors`, niri's own idle, the lid, a resume), so there the waking key is typed. When the monitors wake with no key here, the next key is dropped once. If niri does not deliver the waking key to the lock screen, a password typed within 250 ms of waking loses its first character.
- A PAM service that asks for anything but one hidden prompt (an echoed name, a second secret) fails every check: the password answers only the first hidden prompt. PAM's text and error messages show under the field, cut to 64 characters.
- With `lock.grace` above 0, any key, click, scroll or 4 px of pointer movement on the lock screen unlocks it without a password for that many seconds, only after a lock by the `idle` Module (never `kanade lock`, a lock before sleep or one asked again after a failure). Anyone at the keyboard in that window gets in.
- The session countdown's warning lists only what Kanade knows (a recording, a timer, live Activities) and logind's blocking `shutdown` inhibitors. It cannot know unsaved work in an app, and it is a warning only: nothing stops the restart, power off or log out. See [ADR 0077](https://github.com/0x1d1e/kanade/blob/main/docs/adr/0077-pre-flight-warnings-in-the-session-countdown.md).
- Caffeine's duration does not count time the machine is suspended. An idle daemon sees it only if it honors logind idle inhibitors; hypridle does, but one started while caffeine is already on misses it until it changes. The `idle` Module reads it directly.
- The `idle` Module honors logind idle inhibitors only while it can reach logind on the system bus. Without it, only caffeine and apps' Wayland idle inhibitors hold the stages, and caffeine turned off while the user stays idle counts again only from the next input or idle. See [ADR 0047](https://github.com/0x1d1e/kanade/blob/main/docs/adr/0047-idle-in-the-shell.md).
- The lock screen's layout label shows only with two or more keyboard layouts, and follows what niri says; it can be stale for a moment after niri restarts. It shows no other state: no notification, media or battery.
- Polkit's prompt needs Kanade to be the session's authentication agent, and only one agent can own the name. When another agent, such as polkit-gnome, holds it first, Kanade's registration is refused, nothing shows on screen except the line stderr prints, and it is not retried until the shell restarts. Stop the other agent and restart Kanade. See [ADR 0146](https://github.com/0x1d1e/kanade/blob/main/docs/adr/0146-polkit-auth-on-the-island.md).
